newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA LOOKS TO EXPAND OCTAVIA LINE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA LOOKS TO EXPAND OCTAVIA LINE.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Czech unit Skoda Automobilova a.s. plans to invest another one billion crowns to expand output of its "Octavia" mid-sized car, chairman Vratislav Kulhanek said in an interview with the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Tuesday.
"Through next year we should be capable of producing up to one-third more Octavias than we are able to now at full operation," Kulhanek said.
When the line was launched last September, Skoda forecast producing about 70,000 Octavias in 1997 with total output at 340,000 units, the rest coming from its flagship "Felicia" line of compacts.
Company officials have said they are aiming to produce 500,000 units per year overall by the end of the century.

The Octavia, a curvy mid-sized sedan built in a sparkling new plant in Mlada Boleslav on Volkswagen's platform designed for the 1998 Audi A3 and upgraded Golf, is Skoda's first foray into larger cars since the end of the Communist era.
Kulhanek told Mlada Fronta that Skoda had "a great chance" developing sales to Asian markets and was investing "prudently".
Mlada Fronta, quoting unnamed sources close to Skoda management, said the company was considering launching a line of all-terrain vehicles after the turn of the century.
